sehemu: Part II: Members of Parliament, Constituencies and Election of Members
maudhui: (1) A person shall be qualified for election or appointment as a Member of Parliament if - (a) he is a citizen of the United Republic who has attained the age of twenty-one years and can read and write in Kiswahili or English; (b) he is a member of, and a candidate proposed by, a political party; and (c) within the period of five years before the date of election he has not been convicted by any court of an offence relating to evasion to pay any Government tax. (2) A person shall not be qualified for election or appointment as a Member of Parliament - (a) if he possesses or voluntarily acquires the citizenship of any other country; (b) if it has been formally certified that he is of unsound mind; (c) if he has been convicted by any court and sentenced to death or imprisonment for a term exceeding six months for an offence involving dishonesty; (d) if within five years before the date of a General Election he has been convicted and sentenced to imprisonment for an offence involving dishonesty; (e) if he is not a member of, and a candidate proposed by, a political party; (f) if he has an interest in a Government contract and has contravened the applicable restrictions; (g) if he holds office as a senior officer in the service of the Government; or (h) if he is disqualified from registering as a voter or from voting in an election of Members of Parliament. (3) A person shall not be eligible to contest election as a Member of Parliament representing a constituency at any General Election if at the same time he is a candidate in the election for President, nor shall he be eligible to contest a by-election while he is President. (4) Parliament may enact a law providing for the disqualification of a person from election as a Member of Parliament representing a constituency where that person holds an office connected with the conduct or supervision of elections. (5) Parliament may enact a law providing for the disqualification of a person from election as a Member of Parliament representing a constituency for such period as Parliament may specify, not exceeding five years, where that person is convicted by a court. (6) For the purpose of affording an opportunity to appeal in accordance with law to any person formally certified to be of unsound mind or convicted and sentenced to death or imprisonment, Parliament may enact law making appropriate provision. (7) For the interpretation of paragraphs (c), (d) and (e) of subarticle (2), the following rules shall apply: (a) where a person is sentenced to two or more terms of imprisonment, those sentences shall be treated as separate sentences; (b) where a person is sentenced to imprisonment in default of payment of a fine, that period of imprisonment shall not be taken into account. (8) In paragraph (f) of subarticle (2), "Government contract" means any contractual agreement to which one of the parties is the Government of the United Republic, the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar or any department of either Government. (13) For the avoidance of doubt concerning qualifications for election, the relevant qualifications are those which enable a person to be elected as a Member of Parliament representing a constituency.
